title: Hesap Makinesi
subtitle: Scientific Calculator with Themes & History — First Year CS Project
description: A scientific calculator desktop application built with C# and Windows Forms in 2021, during the first year of computer engineering studies. Features 23 functions including trigonometry, logarithms, factorial and exponentiation, plus calculation history, light/dark theme persistence, and a modern UI powered by the Guna UI library.
longDescription:
Hesap Makinesi is a Windows Forms calculator application developed in 2021 as a first-year computer engineering project. Built with C# and the Guna UI library for a polished, modern interface, the app extends far beyond basic arithmetic into a full scientific calculator.

Scientific operations include square root, exponentiation, cube, factorial, logarithm (log10 and ln), natural exponentiation (exp), reciprocal (1/x), absolute value (|x|), 10^x, the constants π and e, and trigonometric functions (sin, cos, tan, cot). Standard utility buttons cover CE/C for clearing, backspace for last-character deletion, and decimal/sign toggling.

The app saves a history of all performed calculations and displays them in a clean, accessible panel. The light/dark theme preference is persisted across sessions — when the user closes and reopens the app, their last selected theme is remembered and restored automatically.

contentBlocks.heading: Project Overview
contentBlocks.subheading: A First-Year Project That Goes Beyond the Basics
contentBlocks.content:
Hesap Makinesi was developed in 2021 during the first year of computer engineering studies. What started as a calculator project grew into a full-featured scientific calculator with a polished UI, persistent theme support, and calculation history.

The project was built entirely in C# using Windows Forms, with the Guna UI library providing a modern visual layer. It was an early hands-on exploration of event-driven programming, UI design, and mathematical function implementation — and a demonstration that even a beginner project can be taken seriously.

contentBlocks.heading: Full Feature List
contentBlocks.content:
**🔢 Numeric Input (0–9)** — Full numeric keypad for number entry. Each button appends a digit to the current input.

**🧼 CE / C Buttons** — CE clears the last entry (removes the last digit or operation). C resets the entire calculation and clears the display.

**➕ Arithmetic Operations (+, −, ×, ÷, %)** — Addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and percentage calculations.

**= Equals** — Completes the calculation and displays the result.

**√ Square Root** — Calculates the square root of the current number.

**xʸ Exponentiation** — Raises a number to a specified power. Example: 2^3 = 8.

**x³ Cube** — Calculates the cube of the current number. Example: 2³ = 8.

**n! Factorial** — Calculates the factorial of the current number. Example: 5! = 120.

**π (Pi)** — Inserts the mathematical constant π (3.14159...) into the calculation.

**e (Euler's Number)** — Inserts Euler's number (2.71828...) into the calculation.

**log Logarithm** — Calculates the base-10 logarithm of the current number.

**ln Natural Logarithm** — Calculates the natural logarithm (base e) of the current number.

**10ˣ** — Calculates 10 raised to the power of the current number. Example: 10² = 100.

**exp** — Calculates the exponential function (e raised to the power of the current number). Example: exp(1) ≈ 2.71828.

**|x| Absolute Value** — Returns the absolute (non-negative) value of the current number.

**1/x Reciprocal** — Calculates the reciprocal of the current number. Example: 1/5 = 0.2.

**sin, cos, tan, cot** — Trigonometric functions: sine, cosine, tangent, and cotangent of the current angle value.

**+/− Sign Toggle** — Flips the sign of the current number between positive and negative.

**, Decimal Point** — Adds a decimal separator to the current number.

**⌫ Backspace** — Deletes the most recently entered digit or character from the display.

**🎨 Theme Toggle** — Switches between light and dark themes. The selected theme is saved and persisted across sessions.

**🕘 Calculation History** — All calculations performed during the session are logged and displayed in a dedicated history panel for easy review.

contentBlocks.heading: Installation
contentBlocks.content:
**Option 1 — Download the Release (Recommended)**
1. Go to the [Releases page](https://github.com/yasir237/hesap-makinesi/releases/tag/v0.0.1) and download `Hesap.Makinesi.zip`.
2. Extract the ZIP file.
3. Run `HesapMakinesi.exe`.

**Option 2 — Build from Source**
1. Clone the repository:
```
git clone https://github.com/yasir237/hesap-makinesi
```
2. Open the solution in Visual Studio.
3. Restore NuGet packages (Guna UI).
4. Build and run.

> Requires Windows and .NET Framework.
